{"evidence": "# Pi sessions — evidence pack

Corpus: 385 sessions under ~/.pi/agent/sessions, raw 245 MB jsonl.
Total spend: 1.22 B tokens · $1,951.00 · 14,851 tool calls · 581 tool errors.

HEADLINE RATIOS:
- avg cost/session: $5.07 (p50 $1.64, p90 $13.43, p99 $47.88, max $106.19)
- avg tokens/session: 3,160,798
- avg tool calls/session: 39 (p50 20, p90 90, p99 258, max 414)
- parallel-batch / serial-tool turns: 0.127 — 88% of tool turns fire ONE tool, despite system prompt saying batch independents
- workflow tool calls (total, 385 sessions): 0 — exists, never used
- subagent calls: 367 (2.5% of tool calls); only 18% of sessions used subagent at all
- async subagent / subagent: 13% — AGENTS.md says 'default posture: async parallel'; we do opposite
- tool error rate: 3.91% overall
- dup-arg tool calls (exact replay): 537 (3.6%)
- failed retries (err then same tool ≤3 calls): 681; retries/err = 1.17
- sessions on claude-opus-4-7: 361/385 (94%) — virtually no model tiering
- ask_user_question error rate: 22.4% (47/210)
- chrome_evaluate err 27% / chrome_tab err 53%

TOP TOOL USAGE (count, err%): bash 4818 5.6%; read 2816 0.5%; edit 1525 6.3%; todo 1462 1.2%; write 1236 0.2%; ctx_execute 799 6.3%; subagent 367 0.5%; grep 344 0.9%; ls 230 0.4%; ctx_batch_execute 210 6.7%; ask_user_question 210 22.4%; ctx_execute_file 126 4.0%

STOP REASONS: toolUse 12126; stop 1384; error 90; aborted 30; length 1.

TOP COST SESSIONS: $106 test-pi-chrome (317 tc); $85 claude-code-extension (122 tc); $77 implementation-notes loop (414 tc); $48 sticky-note-board (216 tc); $45 subscription tour (136 tc).

TOP DUP-ARG SESSIONS: 89/317 chrome; 77/414 impl-notes; 36/188 impl-notes; 25/219 worktree checkout; 21/149 zuma game.

TOP FAILED-RETRY SESSIONS: 37r/38e chrome; 30r/30e impl-notes; 22r/14e worktree (tool loop-failing); 17r/6e git tests; 16r/8e mobile-app.

ERROR CLUSTERS:
- bash 271 errs: 'sudo: a terminal is required to read the password' (repeated dozens of times — no passwordless sudo); keychain probes; dir-listing fallbacks.
- edit 96 errs: oldText not unique / not found.
- ctx_execute 50 + ctx_batch_execute 14: 'Runtime error: disk I/O error' (SQLite); 'MCP request timeout 120000ms'; 'MCP server has exited'; outdated context-mode warning in EVERY error (v1.0.136 vs available v1.0.151 — 15 minor versions behind, ignored).
- ctx_fetch_and_index 17.8% err: HTTP 404 on guessed doc URLs.
- ask_user_question 22.4% err: schema validation (label>60 chars, duplicate Other row).
- chrome_tab 53% / chrome_evaluate 27% err: extension flaky.

ORCHESTRATION ADOPTION:
- 70/385 (18%) sessions used subagent at all.
- 41/385 (11%) used async subagent.
- 0/385 used workflow tool.
- AGENTS.md standing order: 'Default posture: async parallel'; floor ratio subagent/(write+edit+bash) >0.30.
- ACTUAL cross-corpus ratio: 367/10395 = 0.035 → 10x under floor.

PARALLEL-BATCHING GAP: 11500 tool-using turns; only 1364 (12%) batched >1 tool. System prompt explicitly directs batching of independents.

GOAL-LOOP FRICTION: 26 explicit goal-checkpoint events; 'GOAL STALE' preambles on custom_message channel; same-turn double-checkpoint pattern causing 'yielding'/'resuming' bounces inside one user turn.

NOTABLE PATHOLOGIES:
- test-pi-chrome: 317 tc, $106, 89 dup calls, 37 failed retries — looped chrome extension calls that were returning errors.
- 414-tc impl-notes session: only session to hit 'length' stopReason; never split work via subagent."}

recommendations.title: Block interactive sudo/TTY commands at the Bash tool boundary
recommendations.description: Bash sudo TTY loops are a harness bug: the tool accepts commands that require a controlling TTY (sudo prompts, ssh interactive auth, vim, less without piping) and then hangs until timeout, burning the turn. The model retries because the failure mode looks like 'no output' rather than 'needs TTY'. Fix by pre-flighting commands against a deny/needs-TTY list and returning a structured error that names the cause ('requires TTY; rerun with sudo -n or pipe input') instead of letting the process hang.
recommendations.evidence: Specialist focus explicitly lists 'bash sudo TTY loops' as a recurring cluster across the 385-session pack. Loop shape (repeat-until-timeout) is a harness affordance, not a user choice.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is well understood and the pattern is named in the focus brief; without per-cluster counts from the evidence pack I cannot push above 0.8.
recommendations.risk: False positives on legitimate sudo -n usage; mitigate by allowing -n/--non-interactive and only blocking when stdin is a TTY-requiring prompt.

recommendations.title: Make Edit.oldText anchoring fuzzy-with-confirmation instead of exact-match-or-fail
recommendations.description: Edit oldText anchor failures are a harness bug masquerading as a model bug. The current contract (exact byte match, unique in file) fails on trailing whitespace, CRLF vs LF, tab/space drift, and stale reads after another tool mutated the file. The model then re-Reads and retries, often 3-5 times per edit. Add a two-tier match: exact first, then a whitespace-normalized fallback that returns the canonical match for confirmation. Also auto-invalidate cached file views when any write tool touches the path.
recommendations.evidence: Listed as a top cluster in the specialist focus. The retry-after-Read pattern is a known signature of anchor staleness rather than the model picking bad anchors.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Strong mechanism, well-documented failure mode across coding-agent harnesses generally; named explicitly in this pack's focus.
recommendations.risk: Fuzzy matching could edit the wrong region; require exact match by default and only fall back when there is a single normalized candidate.

recommendations.title: Auto-upgrade ctx_* and surface 'outdated version' as a first-class result, not an error
recommendations.description: ctx_* disk-I/O failures combined with outdated-version warnings are a usage-meets-harness bug: users run stale context-mode installs whose hooks/FTS5 schema drift from the current MCP server, producing opaque disk errors. The model has no clean recovery path and falls back to raw Bash/Read. Bundle a version check into every ctx_* entrypoint that, on mismatch, returns a structured 'upgrade required' result with the exact command, and gate destructive ops behind it. Treat repeated disk-I/O errors in one session as a doctor trigger.
recommendations.evidence: Focus brief calls out 'ctx_* disk-I/O + outdated version' as a paired signal — the co-occurrence is the tell that version drift is causing the I/O errors, not unrelated disk pressure.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Paired signal is strong directional evidence; without per-session version stamps I cannot confirm the proportion attributable to drift vs genuine I/O.
recommendations.risk: Adds a startup check cost on every ctx_* call; cache the version handshake per session.

recommendations.title: Treat MCP timeouts as retry-with-backoff at the harness layer, not as model-visible failures
recommendations.description: MCP timeouts are a harness bug. When an MCP server stalls, the current behavior bubbles a generic timeout to the model, which then re-issues the same call (often with the same payload) or abandons the tool and switches to a worse alternative (e.g., dropping ctx_search for raw Bash greps). Add a single transparent retry with jittered backoff and a circuit-breaker that, after 2 consecutive timeouts on the same MCP, returns a structured 'server-degraded; fallback X suggested' instead of opaque timeout text.
recommendations.evidence: Listed as a cluster. The downstream-substitution pattern (model abandoning ctx_* for Bash) is also implied by the ctx_* cluster co-occurrence.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is plausible and matches general MCP timeout behavior; lacking per-server timeout counts I keep this in the 0.7 band.
recommendations.risk: Hidden retries can mask real outages; emit a telemetry event on every retry so the breaker state is observable.

recommendations.title: Enforce ask_user_question schema at construction time with a typed builder, not at submission
recommendations.description: ask_user_question schema failures (label length >60, header >16, missing description, authoring banned 'Other'/'Type something.' rows, options outside 2-4) are a usage bug created by a harness affordance: the schema is enforced only at submit time, so the model wastes a tool call to discover the violation and then re-emits the whole questionnaire. Two fixes, both harness-side: (a) ship a JSON-schema-validated dry-run preview tool, and (b) when rejection happens, return the exact offending field path and the trimmed/legal value so the model can repair in one turn instead of regenerating.
recommendations.evidence: Named cluster in the focus brief. The shape (regenerate-entire-questionnaire-on-reject) is symptomatic of insufficient error locality, which is a harness contract issue.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is direct and the fix is mechanical; confidence capped without the actual rejection-rate number from the pack.
recommendations.risk: None significant; field-level errors are strictly more informative than the current global reject.

recommendations.title: Quarantine chrome-extension flakiness behind an explicit liveness probe and degrade to fetch_content
recommendations.description: Chrome-extension flakiness (Gemini Web, Exa-via-extension paths) is a tooling bug whose symptom in sessions is partial results or silent zero-result returns that the model treats as 'no information available' rather than 'tool broken'. Add a liveness probe at the start of any extension-backed call; on failure, automatically degrade to fetch_content + a direct provider API (Perplexity/Exa direct), and surface the degradation in the response so the model does not over-trust an empty answer.
recommendations.evidence: Listed as a cluster in the focus. Silent-empty failure mode is consistent with browser-extension session loss (login expiry, tab eviction), which is a known class.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Directional — mechanism is plausible but I do not have per-provider failure counts from the pack to separate extension flakiness from genuine zero-result queries.
recommendations.risk: Liveness probes add latency to every search; cache the probe result for the session and only re-probe on first failure.

recommendations.title: Hard tool-call ceiling with forced summarization at p99
recommendations.description: Introduce a hard circuit breaker at ~260 tool calls (current p99) that auto-triggers a forced-summarization checkpoint: the harness injects a synthetic system turn asking the model to (a) write a compact state digest to disk, (b) declare remaining work as a todo list, and (c) hand off to a fresh-context continuation. Sessions reaching 414 tool calls (observed max) are almost certainly in pathological loops rather than doing 414 calls of useful work; the long tail past p99 is where the waste concentrates.
recommendations.evidence: p99 = 258 tool calls, max = 414 across N=385 sessions. The gap between p99 and max (~60% headroom above p99) indicates a heavy upper tail consistent with runaway loops rather than legitimately large jobs.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Clear distributional signal (p99 vs max gap) with a believable mechanism (loops dominate the tail). Lacking per-session outcome labels to confirm the tail sessions are unproductive, hence not 0.9+.
recommendations.risk: False positives on legitimately large refactors/migrations. Mitigate by making the breaker a forced-checkpoint (summarize + continue in fresh context) rather than a hard kill, and by exempting sessions whose recent N calls show diverse tool/arg signatures.

recommendations.title: Duplicate-argument replay detector with exponential backoff and escalation
recommendations.description: Hash every tool call by (tool_name, normalized_args). On the 2nd identical replay within a session, return the cached prior result plus a system note 'duplicate call suppressed — prior result inlined'. On the 3rd, hard-block the call and force a planning turn ('you are repeating the same call; state your new hypothesis before continuing'). On the 4th, escalate to forced summarization + handoff (LSP-1 path).
recommendations.evidence: 537 duplicate-arg replays corpus-wide across 385 sessions = ~1.4 replays/session average, concentrated in long sessions. Each replay is by definition zero new information for nonzero token cost.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is unambiguous (identical args → identical result for pure tools) and the count is large. Slight uncertainty only because some tools are non-idempotent (Bash, network fetches) and need allowlisting.
recommendations.risk: Non-idempotent tools (Bash, fetch, time-sensitive reads) must be excluded from auto-cache or only soft-warned. A naive hash on Bash 'ls' would over-suppress. Maintain a per-tool idempotency flag.

recommendations.title: Failed-retry loop breaker with mandatory hypothesis-change gate
recommendations.description: Track consecutive failures per (tool, target). After 3 failed attempts on the same target (file path, command, URL), block the 4th attempt and inject: 'You have failed 3× on <target> with errors: [...]. State a new hypothesis or escalate. Repeating the same approach is disallowed.' Pair with a 'rubber-duck' forced reasoning turn before the next mutating call is permitted.
recommendations.evidence: 681 failed-retry loops corpus-wide (~1.77/session). This is the single largest waste category in the pack — failed retries cost full tool latency + reasoning tokens with negative information value (they reinforce a wrong model).
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Multiple converging signals: count is highest of the three pathologies, mechanism (sunk-cost retry without hypothesis change) is well-documented in agent failure modes, and the fix is mechanically simple to gate on.
recommendations.risk: Legitimate flaky-network retries get blocked. Mitigate by distinguishing transient errors (timeout, 5xx, EAGAIN) — those get free retries with backoff — from deterministic errors (file not found, permission denied, syntax error) which trigger the gate immediately.

recommendations.title: Sliding-window context compactor triggered by tool-call density, not token count
recommendations.description: Trigger forced compaction when tool-calls-per-recent-window exceeds a threshold (e.g. >40 calls in last 50 turns with <2 distinct files touched), independent of token budget. This catches 'thrash' sessions before they hit token limits. Compaction writes an implementation-notes-style HTML log of decisions + open questions, then resets working context to: original task + digest + last 5 turns.
recommendations.evidence: p99 258 / max 414 with 537 duplicate replays + 681 failed retries implies long sessions are dominated by low-diversity churn, not legitimate context growth. Token-based compaction misses this because thrashing sessions are token-efficient per call but useless per call.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Directional — the diversity metric (calls per unique target) is the right shape, but exact thresholds need calibration against per-session productivity labels not visible in this pack.
recommendations.risk: Compaction itself can lose state. Make it append-only (preserve original todos, file list, decisions) and reversible via a 'restore prior context' command for the parent.

recommendations.title: Per-session budget surfaced to the model with degradation tiers
recommendations.description: Inject a live 'session budget' status line into every system turn: 'tool_calls: 187/250 soft / 350 hard. duplicates_suppressed: 4. failed_retries: 7.' Model behavior shifts measurably when it can see its own runway. Pair with explicit degradation tiers in the system prompt: at 60% budget, prefer batched tools (ctx_batch_execute) over single calls; at 80%, switch to summarize-and-handoff mode; at 95%, no new exploratory calls — only finalize.
recommendations.evidence: p99 = 258 tool calls indicates models routinely operate without budget awareness. The duplicate-replay count (537) corroborates that models don't track their own prior actions well — explicit metrics in context fix the awareness gap cheaply.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Plausible mechanism with precedent (visible budgets change planning behavior in agent literature), but no direct A/B in this pack confirming magnitude of effect.
recommendations.risk: Adds ~30 tokens/turn overhead. Negligible relative to one duplicate tool call saved.

recommendations.title: Auto-fanout escalation when single-session call count crosses p95
recommendations.description: When a session crosses the p95 tool-call mark, the harness offers (or auto-invokes, configurable) a fanout: spawn a fresh-context planner subagent that reads the current session digest and returns a structured plan, then the parent either executes the plan or hands off to a worker subagent. This converts pathological linear sessions into bounded delegations matching the global AGENTS.md 'orchestration shape' rule.
recommendations.evidence: p99 258 / max 414 long tail strongly suggests sessions that would have benefited from a midway re-plan. The standing pi-subagents discipline already prescribes this for multi-file work; the harness can enforce it when in-session metrics indicate the parent has lost the plot.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism plausible and aligns with documented best practice, but evidence pack doesn't directly measure orchestration ratios or counterfactual outcomes from auto-fanout.
recommendations.risk: Forced fanout mid-session can lose tacit context the parent had built up. Make it opt-in by default (parent gets a 'consider fanout' nudge), opt-out after observing positive outcomes.

recommendations.title: Evidence pack missing — instrument per-session cost telemetry before further optimization
recommendations.description: The provided EVIDENCE PACK was literally 'undefined', so no per-tool, per-model, or per-session cost breakdown of the $1,951 was available to this analyst. Before any tiering or pruning change is justified, the harness needs a persisted cost ledger: (session_id, tool, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_tokens, cost_usd, ts). Without this, every other recommendation here is speculative.
recommendations.evidence: EVIDENCE PACK value passed to this specialist = 'undefined'. Only the aggregate ($1,951 across 385 sessions ≈ $5.07/session avg) is known. No tool-level or model-level distribution provided.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a cost-logging hook that appends a JSONL row per LLM call and per tool call into ~/.pi/telemetry/cost.jsonl, then add a `pi cost` command that pivots by session, tool, model, and tier. Re-run this analysis against the real pack.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Directly observable: the pack passed in is empty. Cannot responsibly recommend cuts against $1,951 without seeing where it landed.
recommendations.risk: None; pure observability. Mild disk growth.

recommendations.title: Default new agents to a medium tier and force explicit opt-in for 'big' tier
recommendations.description: Industry-standard pattern for coding-agent harnesses (and pi's own workflow tier system: small/medium/big) is that untagged agents silently fall back to medium, but synthesis/judgment agents drift to big because authors copy templates. With $5.07/session average, even a 20% share of sessions routed to Opus-class models when Sonnet/Haiku would suffice is plausibly responsible for the majority of spend. Make 'big' opt-in with a one-line justification in the agent definition.
recommendations.evidence: Aggregate $1,951 / 385 sessions = $5.07 avg/session. pi system prompt explicitly documents tier fallback to medium and that 'big' should be reserved for synthesis/judgment. No tier-distribution data was provided to refute or confirm misuse, but the mechanism is well-known.
recommendations.concreteAction: In the workflow runtime, log a warning when an agent runs on big tier without opts.tier='big' set explicitly. Add a `pi workflows audit` command that lists agents by tier and flags untagged big-tier usage.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is plausible and documented in the harness itself, but no tier-distribution evidence was supplied. Directional only.
recommendations.risk: Some legitimate synthesis agents may need big-tier; opt-in friction is the tradeoff. Mitigate with clear error message + suggested tier change.

recommendations.title: Cap parent-session context growth via mandatory ctx_execute / ctx_batch_execute for tool outputs >20 lines
recommendations.description: Parent sessions in long pi runs accumulate verbatim tool output (logs, greps, file reads) in the conversation, which gets re-sent on every subsequent turn. With Anthropic-family pricing on long-context turns and 385 sessions, even modest per-turn bloat compounds into a large share of the $1,951. context-mode's whole thesis is exactly this; enforce it via a PreToolUse hook that rejects raw Bash on commands likely to emit >20 lines.
recommendations.evidence: context-mode skill ships and is active in this very session; its 'MANDATORY RULE' explicitly targets this failure mode. No per-session token-distribution data was provided, but the mechanism (quadratic-ish cost in turn count × context size) is mathematically certain.
recommendations.concreteAction: Promote context-mode's PreToolUse routing from advisory to default-on for new installs; add a per-session 'context bytes returned' counter to ctx_stats and surface it in session summaries.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is rock-solid and the harness already ships the mitigation. Lacking the actual token distribution prevents a higher score.
recommendations.risk: Some users may find forced routing annoying; keep an escape hatch.

recommendations.title: Prefer async subagent fanout over inline parent work for multi-file tasks (cost via context isolation)
recommendations.description: Per the project's AGENTS.md, multi-file changes are supposed to be delegated to subagents. The cost angle (beyond the orchestration-quality angle the rule was written for) is that subagent children run in fresh/forked context, so their large file reads and tool outputs do NOT pollute the parent's growing context. A parent that does the work inline pays for those tokens on every subsequent turn for the rest of the session.
recommendations.evidence: AGENTS.md mandates subagent dispatch as 'level −1' for multi-file work. The self-grading rule (subagent:Write ratio > 0.30) implies the author has observed the failure mode. No per-session ratio data was provided.
recommendations.concreteAction: Log the subagent:Write ratio per session and surface it in `pi cost` output alongside session cost; sessions with low ratio AND high cost are the highest-leverage cleanup targets.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Strong mechanism, repo-level policy already agrees, but no quantitative link to the $1,951 was provided.
recommendations.risk: Subagent dispatch itself costs tokens; the win is only real on tasks with >2 turns of follow-up in the parent.

recommendations.title: Enable prompt-caching for the global AGENTS.md / system prompt block
recommendations.description: The system prompt in this session alone is ~30KB (skill listings, AGENTS.md, tool descriptions). Across 385 sessions with multiple turns each, re-sending this uncached is a meaningful share of input-token spend. Anthropic prompt caching cuts cached-prefix input cost ~90%. If pi is not already setting cache_control on the stable system-prompt prefix, this is a near-free win.
recommendations.evidence: Direct observation of the system prompt size in this session (skills block alone enumerates ~25 skills with descriptions). 385 sessions × multi-turn × ~30KB prefix is a non-trivial denominator of $1,951.
recommendations.concreteAction: Verify the Anthropic client wrapper sets cache_control: {type:'ephemeral'} on the stable system-prompt block and on the skills/AGENTS.md region. Add a unit test that the cached prefix hash is stable across turns.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is well-understood; pricing impact is documented by the provider. Confidence not higher because I can't confirm from the evidence whether caching is already enabled.
recommendations.risk: If already enabled, no harm; just verify.

recommendations.title: Add a hard per-session $ budget with graceful degradation
recommendations.description: $5.07 average across 385 sessions almost certainly hides a long tail — a handful of runaway sessions (workflow loops, review-loop without convergence, autoresearch that didn't terminate) likely account for a disproportionate share of the $1,951. The workflow tool already exposes tokenBudget; extend that to session level and degrade to smaller tier / fewer parallel reviewers when 75% of budget is consumed.
recommendations.evidence: $1,951 / 385 = $5.07 mean. Without the distribution it's an inference, but coding-agent cost distributions are reliably long-tailed (p99 ≫ mean) across every published dataset.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add PI_SESSION_BUDGET_USD env var; emit a soft warning at 50%, hard tier-downgrade at 75%, refuse new agent() calls at 100% with a clear message to the user.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Distribution shape is inferred from prior knowledge of agent-cost telemetry, not from the supplied pack.
recommendations.risk: Hard caps may interrupt useful work; surface clearly and let users override per-session.

recommendations.title: Move the batching directive from system-prompt prose into a pre-tool-call checklist
recommendations.description: The system prompt currently states 'if you intend to call multiple tools and there are no dependencies... make all of the independent calls in the same block' as a single sentence buried near the end of a long instruction blob. At a 0.127 parallel/serial ratio (~1 in 8 eligible call sites batched), the rule is being read but not retrieved at decision time. Re-shape it as a structured pre-call checklist the model is instructed to run silently before EVERY tool block: (1) list intended calls, (2) mark dependencies, (3) emit independents in one block. This converts a passive norm into an active decision step.
recommendations.evidence: 0.127 parallel/serial ratio across 385 sessions despite explicit system-prompt directive — indicates instruction is present but not salient at the moment of action.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Strong single signal (large N=385, explicit instruction already present so the gap is clearly retrieval/salience, not knowledge). Mechanism — recency/placement effects on long-context instruction following — is well established.
recommendations.risk: Adds tokens to every turn; minor latency. Could over-batch and cause dependency bugs if checklist is sloppy — mitigated by step (2).
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a short '<batching_checklist>' block near the END of the system prompt (recency-weighted), worded as imperative steps the model must mentally execute before opening any <function_calls> block. Include 1 positive example (3 independent reads batched) and 1 negative example (read-then-edit kept serial).

recommendations.title: Add 2-3 worked few-shot examples of batched independent tool calls
recommendations.description: The current instruction is abstract ('make all independent calls in the same block') with one minimal example block showing 2 calls to the same hypothetical tool. Models pattern-match to examples far more reliably than to rules. The 0.127 ratio is consistent with 'example-driven floor': the model batches roughly when the situation looks like the lone example. Provide concrete examples for the highest-frequency batchable shapes in this harness: (a) multiple Read calls on different files, (b) Read + Grep + find_files for exploration, (c) multiple ctx_execute_file calls.
recommendations.evidence: Single abstract example in system prompt + 0.127 batching rate across 385 sessions. The example shown uses a fictional 'example_complex_tool' rather than real tools the model will actually call.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Few-shot effects on tool-use formatting are very well documented; the current example is demonstrably weak (uses a fake tool name, single shape). Mechanism is direct.
recommendations.risk: Slightly longer system prompt. Examples must use real tool names from THIS harness or they'll mislead.
recommendations.concreteAction: Replace the 'example_complex_tool' block with 2-3 examples using real tools (Read x3, Grep+find_files+Read, ctx_batch_execute usage). Annotate each with 'these are independent → one block'.

recommendations.title: Instrument and surface a per-turn batching metric to the model via a system reminder
recommendations.description: Models cannot self-correct on metrics they don't see. Inject a lightweight system-reminder after turns where the model issued ≥2 sequential independent tool calls that could have been batched (detected post-hoc: no data dependency between call N's output and call N+1's arguments). Reminder text: 'Last turn: 3 independent tool calls were issued serially. They could have been one block.' This creates an in-context feedback loop.
recommendations.evidence: 0.127 ratio is stable across 385 sessions — suggests no corrective pressure exists during a session. Without feedback, models drift to the easier serial-thinking default.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism plausible (in-context corrections measurably change behavior), but requires harness work to detect 'independent' calls reliably; false positives could annoy or confuse. Directional rather than proven.
recommendations.risk: Misclassifying dependent calls as independent will train bad batching. Need conservative independence detector.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a harness-side detector: if call N+1's arguments contain no string from call N's stdout AND tools are read-only/idempotent, emit a system reminder next turn. Log a 'batching_score' to session telemetry to re-measure.

recommendations.title: Promote ctx_batch_execute and parallel-shaped tools above their serial siblings in tool descriptions
recommendations.description: The harness already ships ctx_batch_execute, fff_multi_grep, and web_search.queries[]. These are the batched forms of ctx_execute, Grep, and web_search.query. Tool descriptions currently treat the singular form as primary and the plural as a variant. Invert this: make the batched tool the documented default, and add 'Prefer this over single-call X when you have ≥2 independent items' to each batched tool's first sentence. Tool descriptions are read at every turn — placement here is high-leverage.
recommendations.evidence: Harness exposes batched variants (ctx_batch_execute, fff_multi_grep, web_search.queries) yet 0.127 ratio persists. The affordances exist; the steering toward them does not.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Direct mechanism: tool descriptions are the model's primary discovery surface. Existing batched tools mean zero implementation cost. Single strong signal.
recommendations.risk: Users writing single-item queries might get pushed toward batch tool with awkward 1-element arrays. Mitigate with 'use single form only when N=1'.
recommendations.concreteAction: Edit description fields of ctx_batch_execute, fff_multi_grep, and web_search to lead with the batch use-case. Add to ctx_execute description: 'For ≥2 independent commands, use ctx_batch_execute instead.'

recommendations.title: Add a planning-prompt convention: emit an explicit 'parallelizable set' before any multi-step block
recommendations.description: When the model uses todo or thinks out loud before acting, it tends to list steps as an ordered sequence ('first I'll read X, then Y, then Z'). This linguistic framing leaks into tool-call structure — sequenced thinking produces sequenced calls. Add a system-prompt convention: when planning, end the plan with a one-line 'Parallel set: {tools that can fire together}' before opening the function_calls block. This bridges the gap between sequential natural-language planning and parallel execution.
recommendations.evidence: 0.127 ratio + heavy use of todo/planning tools in pi sessions. Sequential planning prose is a known driver of sequential tool emission; current prompt doesn't counter it.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism plausible and supported by chain-of-thought research, but specific intervention is novel — would benefit from A/B data before declaring a win.
recommendations.risk: Could add planning verbosity. If model parrots the convention without actually parallelizing, no gain.
recommendations.concreteAction: Append to system prompt: 'When you have planned 2+ next actions, before calling tools, identify which have no input dependency on each other. Emit those in one function_calls block.' Pair with PB-2's examples.

recommendations.title: Detect and dedupe sequential same-tool calls at the harness level with a soft block
recommendations.description: As a backstop to prompt-level fixes (PB-1, PB-2, PB-5): if the model issues 2 consecutive turns each containing a single Read/Grep/ctx_execute call with no intervening data dependency, the harness inserts a system note 'Two sequential single-tool turns detected — these could have been one batched turn. Continue.' This is non-blocking but creates pressure. Stronger version: silently coalesce them in telemetry to measure the true 'wanted serial but did serial' rate vs the 'wanted parallel but did serial' rate.
recommendations.evidence: 0.127 ratio aggregates two failure modes (forgot-to-batch vs. couldn't-batch). Without separating them, prompt fixes target a blurry distribution. Harness-side detection is the only way to separate.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Diagnostic value is high; behavioral effect on model is speculative. Directional — needs implementation to see if signal is actionable.
recommendations.risk: Adds harness complexity. Soft-block messages can confuse the model if dependency analysis is wrong.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add session-level metric: % of turns containing exactly 1 tool call where that tool's args could have been merged with the previous turn's single-tool call. Report alongside the parallel/serial ratio in the existing dashboard to pinpoint whether the problem is 'never batches' or 'batches the wrong things'.

recommendations.title: Convert AGENTS.md floor rules into runtime-enforced preflight gates, not prose
recommendations.description: The HARD RULE ('first action on multi-file change must be a subagent dispatch') and the >0.30 floor ratio are stated as prose in a symlinked markdown file. Prose in the system prompt is advisory under tempo pressure — by the time the agent has read a detailed plan and is mid-todo, the rule is a memory lookup competing with momentum. Replace 'standing order text' with a harness preflight: when the agent calls Write/Edit/Bash-mutate and the session has zero prior subagent dispatches AND the change touches >1 file or creates files in >1 directory, the tool call is rejected with a structured error pointing to the rule and offering a one-call escape (explicit ack token). This converts a soft norm into a typed contract.
recommendations.evidence: Specialist framing reports floor ratios missed 10x despite AGENTS.md being symlinked to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md — i.e. delivery is not the problem, the rule lands every session and is still ignored. Aggregated over 385 sessions, 10x miss rate on a stated floor is a mechanism signal, not a coverage signal.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a PreToolUse hook for Write/Edit/Bash that counts prior subagent dispatches in the session and inspects pending file targets; block first multi-file mutation with a remediation message that names /parallel-research, /parallel-context-build, or scout-async as the cheapest unblock. Provide an explicit `--ack-skip-orchestration <reason>` token to bypass, logged for self-grading.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Strong single signal (10x miss despite universal delivery) with a clear mechanism (prose loses to tempo). Confidence capped below 0.9 because the underlying per-session breakdown isn't in the pack — possible the 10x is dominated by a few session types where a gate would be wrong.
recommendations.risk: False positives on legitimate single-file or investigative work that the heuristic misreads as multi-file. Mitigation: gate fires only on the FIRST mutation of the session and only when target set is multi-file; subsequent edits are unblocked.

recommendations.title: Make 'choose orchestration shape' a structured todo template, not a free-text instruction
recommendations.description: AGENTS.md tells the agent to make 'choose orchestration shape' the first todo. In practice, under conversational tempo ('go ahead', 'just ship it'), the agent skips writing that todo and starts editing. The fix is to stop relying on the agent to author the todo and instead inject it: on session start for any task that smells like implementation (verbs: build/refactor/migrate/add/fix-across), the harness pre-creates a pending todo with subject 'choose orchestration shape' and forces it to in_progress before any mutating tool fires.
recommendations.evidence: Specialist focus calls out tempo-pressure skipping. The rule exists in the prompt verbatim ('the first todo must literally be choose orchestration shape') and is still skipped — this is the classic prose-vs-state failure mode. 385-session base supports treating this as systemic, not random.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a session-init hook that pattern-matches the opening user turn for implementation verbs and seeds todo #1 = 'choose orchestration shape' (activeForm: 'choosing orchestration shape'), with a metadata flag the PreToolUse gate (SO-1) checks. Closing this todo requires either a logged subagent dispatch or an explicit shape=single-file/conversational tag.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Same mechanism as SO-1 (prose→state), high-confidence direction, but slightly speculative on the exact verb-matcher quality without seeing the prompt distribution in the pack.
recommendations.risk: Annoying overhead on genuinely trivial tasks. Mitigation: cheap escape via tagging the todo single-file; the cost is one todo update, not a dispatch.

recommendations.title: Fix GOAL-STALE in-turn bouncing by snapshotting goal state at turn start
recommendations.description: GOAL-STALE bouncing within a single turn indicates the goal-loop is re-reading goal state mid-turn and observing changes (either from concurrent writers, file mtime races, or the agent's own writes invalidating cache). Within-turn instability of standing-order-adjacent state poisons every downstream decision: the agent reads goal A, plans against it, then re-reads and gets goal A' and either retries or no-ops. The fix is to take a single immutable snapshot of goal+standing-orders at turn entry, expose it to every tool that needs it for the duration of the turn, and only revalidate at turn boundary.
recommendations.evidence: Specialist focus explicitly cites 'Goal-loop GOAL-STALE bouncing within turns' as a top symptom across the 385-session aggregate. 'Within turns' is the diagnostic — it isolates the problem to mid-turn re-reads, not session-to-session drift.
recommendations.concreteAction: In the goal subsystem, add a turn-scoped read-through cache keyed by (sessionId, turnId). get_goal and any standing-orders read returns the snapshot for the whole turn. Mutations (update_goal, pause_goal, apply_goal_tweak) invalidate at turn end, not mid-turn. Log every GOAL-STALE event with prior+current hash so the residual rate is measurable.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Clear named symptom with a clean mechanism (mid-turn re-read race). Confidence under 0.85 because the pack doesn't include a count of GOAL-STALE events or the writers responsible; the fix shape is right even if the exact race source needs one more debugging pass.
recommendations.risk: Stale snapshots could mask a legitimate user-driven goal change made mid-turn via another session. Mitigation: snapshot is per-turn-per-session, not global; cross-session edits are still seen on the next turn boundary.

recommendations.title: Replace the >0.30 self-grading ratio with a real-time counter surfaced in the TUI
recommendations.description: Self-grading 'at the end of any implementation session' is the wrong feedback loop — by the time the agent self-grades, the work is done and the lesson is paid for. Surface the live ratio (subagent dispatches / mutating Write+Edit+Bash calls) in the TUI status line continuously. When the ratio drops below 0.10 with >5 mutations logged, flip the status indicator to a warning state. This converts a post-hoc reflection into a tight in-loop signal, the same mechanism that made todo lists actually work.
recommendations.evidence: AGENTS.md prescribes the ratio (>0.30 target, <0.10 flag-explicitly) but the 10x floor-miss rate means self-grading is not catching it in flight. 385 sessions is enough N to assert that 'reflect at the end' is not the right placement for this signal.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a session-scoped counter to pi's TUI. Tools already log dispatches; add a derived metric and a chip in the status bar. Optional: emit a soft nudge (chat-level, not blocking) when ratio < 0.10 and >5 mutations have fired, with a one-click '/parallel-review last diff' shortcut.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Directional with strong precedent (todo state visibility worked). The exact threshold (5 mutations, 0.10) is calibrated from the AGENTS.md numbers, not the evidence pack — confidence reflects that gap.
recommendations.risk: Noise if the chip nags on legitimate single-writer work. Mitigation: chip is informational; the nudge only fires once per session.

recommendations.title: Resolve the context-mode vs pi-subagents conflict in the runtime, not just the prose
recommendations.description: AGENTS.md resolves the context-mode/pi-subagents conflict textually ('subagent dispatch is level -1') but both extensions ship competing 'MANDATORY' framings into the same prompt. When two extensions both claim mandatory authority over tool choice, the agent under tempo defaults to whichever tool is most ergonomic in the moment — typically ctx_batch_execute, because it's one call and feels productive. The fix is to encode the precedence in the hook layer: when a PreToolUse hook sees ctx_batch_execute fired on a session with no prior subagent dispatch AND the planned commands look like implementation reconnaissance (>3 commands, mixed read/inspect), it should redirect with a structured suggestion ('this looks like scout work; dispatch a scout subagent instead?').
recommendations.evidence: AGENTS.md explicitly documents the conflict and the 10x miss rate aggregates across 385 sessions, which strongly suggests prose-level resolution is failing. The 'hand reaches for ctx_batch_execute' pattern is named in AGENTS.md as the wrong-decision-tree firing.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a PreToolUse hook on ctx_batch_execute with the same session-mutation-count heuristic as SO-1. Suggest (don't block) a scout dispatch. Log accept/reject so the policy can be tuned.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Plausible mechanism, but the pack doesn't separate 'ctx_batch_execute used correctly for processing' from 'ctx_batch_execute used as a delegation substitute', so this is directional. Suggesting rather than blocking keeps the false-positive cost low.
recommendations.risk: Hook noise if the heuristic over-fires on legitimate context-mode usage. Suggest-only mode plus accept/reject logging keeps the risk bounded and measurable.

recommendations.title: Treat conversational tempo as a feature, not a bypass — add a 'tempo mode' explicit flag
recommendations.description: AGENTS.md tells the agent that 'cool let's do it' / 'just ship it' is NOT an override of standing orders. This is asking the agent to disregard the strongest local signal (the user just told me to go) in favor of a global rule. That's a hard ask under any model. Instead, add a first-class 'tempo mode' the user can opt into explicitly (slash command or env flag) that documents the tradeoff: tempo mode skips orchestration floor, logs every skip, and ends with a session report listing what would have been orchestrated. Make the bypass legible instead of contested.
recommendations.evidence: AGENTS.md HARD RULE point 4 explicitly calls out that conversational tempo is being used as a bypass and that this should not work — yet the 10x miss rate over 385 sessions says the prohibition isn't holding. When prose says 'don't do X' and X keeps happening, X usually has structural pull the prose can't overcome.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add /tempo-mode (toggle) and /tempo-mode-report. While active, the SO-1 gate is downgraded from block to log. End-of-session, emit a short report listing the would-have-been-orchestrated shapes. This honors the user's signal while preserving the data the >0.30 self-grade needs.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is plausible (legible bypass beats contested bypass) but this is a policy proposal more than a measured fix; the evidence pack doesn't quantify how often tempo-driven skips are the dominant skip mode vs. e.g. forgetfulness. Directional confidence only.
recommendations.risk: Could become an always-on escape hatch that erodes the floor entirely. Mitigation: tempo mode is per-session, off by default, and the report itself is a soft enforcement mechanism.

recommendations.title: Move the orchestration mandate from AGENTS.md prose into a runtime pre-tool gate
recommendations.description: AGENTS.md declares a HARD RULE that the first action on any multi-file change must be a scout/researcher subagent and that the subagent:direct-mutate ratio must exceed 0.30. Observed: workflow=0% of 385 sessions, subagent=18%, async=11% — i.e. the mandate is being read and ignored. Prose-level standing orders lose to conversational tempo ("go ahead", "just ship it"), which AGENTS.md itself anticipates in HARD RULE point 4. The fix is to stop relying on the model remembering: add a PreToolUse hook (same shape as context-mode's routing hook) that, when the first Write/Edit/Bash-mutate of a session touches >1 directory or creates >1 new file, blocks the call and returns a structured error telling the agent to dispatch a scout first. Hook-level enforcement is the only thing that survives short user prompts.
recommendations.evidence: workflow=0/385 (0%), subagent=70/385 (18%), async=43/385 (11%); target ratio >0.30 missed by ~12pp on the subagent axis alone; AGENTS.md explicitly names the failure mode ("conversational tempo is NOT a license to skip") yet adoption is still near floor.
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a pi extension hook `orchestration-gate` that intercepts Write/Edit/Bash on session-first multi-file mutations and returns `{ block: true, reason: 'standing-orders: dispatch scout first', suggested: subagent({ agent: "scout", async: true, task: ... }) }`. Ship it disabled-by-default behind a config flag so power users can opt out.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Single strong signal (0% workflow, 18% subagent across N=385) plus a clear mechanism (prose mandates lose to tempo) plus a precedent that already works in this codebase (context-mode's PreToolUse routing). Not 0.9+ because we don't have per-session evidence on WHY each session skipped — could partly be task mix.
recommendations.risk: False positives on legitimate single-developer quick edits will be annoying; mitigate with a one-key bypass and a heuristic that only fires on session-first multi-file mutations, not every edit.

recommendations.title: Replace `subagent({ tasks: [...] })` as the default surface with named recipe slash-commands
recommendations.description: The `subagent` tool's JSON-schema surface is enormous (chain/parallel/expand/collect/acceptance/control/...). Cognitive cost of authoring a correct parallel dispatch from scratch is high enough that the agent reverts to Write/Edit. AGENTS.md already lists the canonical recipes (`/parallel-review`, `/review-loop`, `/parallel-research`, `/parallel-context-build`, `/parallel-handoff-plan`, `/parallel-cleanup`, full Clarify→Plan→Implement→Review→Fix) but they are documentation, not first-class tool calls. Promote each recipe to a saved chain/workflow with a one-line invocation so the agent's path of least resistance becomes orchestration rather than direct edits. Workflow=0% strongly suggests the `workflow` tool's required `script` parameter (raw JS, meta export, phase rules, tier tagging, 20+ guidelines) is too expensive to author on demand.
recommendations.evidence: workflow=0/385 despite being the explicitly recommended fan-out primitive; subagent=18% — non-zero but well below the 30%+ ratio AGENTS.md mandates; the `workflow` tool's system-prompt section is the longest of any tool (~25 bullet points of constraints).
recommendations.concreteAction: Ship 6 saved chains/workflows matching the named recipes. Each invocable as `await workflow('parallel-review', { target: ... })` or as a slash command. Cut the surface the agent has to author from "write a 40-line JS script with meta export and tier tags" to "name a recipe and pass a target".
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Workflow=0 is an unambiguous signal that the current authoring surface is unused. Mechanism (high friction → fallback to direct edits) is well-established in tool-design literature. Slightly under 0.9 because we lack telemetry on aborted/half-written workflow attempts.
recommendations.risk: Saved recipes can drift from the rules in AGENTS.md; pin them to the same skill file and add a smoke test.

recommendations.title: Make async the default for subagent dispatch, not an opt-in flag
recommendations.description: AGENTS.md says "Default posture: async parallel" and "Foreground is the explicit opt-out, not the default." The data says the opposite is happening: of 18% of sessions that used subagent, only 11/18 ≈ 61% used async — and across all 385 sessions, async appears in only 11%. So even the agents that DO delegate are blocking the parent ~40% of the time. The fix is at the tool-definition layer: flip `async` to default true for `subagent` (matching the `workflow` tool, which already defaults background=true) and require an explicit `async: false` for the blocking case. This makes the documented default match the API default.
recommendations.evidence: subagent=18%, async=11% → roughly 7pp of subagent calls are foreground, despite the standing order; `workflow` tool already defaults background:true and the system prompt explicitly contrasts the two defaults.
recommendations.concreteAction: Change `subagent`'s effective default for SINGLE/PARALLEL/CHAIN modes from foreground to async:true. Update the system-prompt guideline that currently says `async (default: false)`. Add a one-time migration note for any downstream skill that assumed sync.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Clear single signal (11% / 18% = 61% async-share within delegators) and an obvious mechanism (defaults dominate behavior). Not higher because some foreground use is legitimate (quick one-shot reviewer where the parent has nothing else to do).
recommendations.risk: Breaks any skill that assumed synchronous return; mitigate with one release of dual-default behavior gated by config.

recommendations.title: Inject an orchestration self-grade into the end-of-turn summary
recommendations.description: AGENTS.md asks for a self-grading ratio at session end ("ratio of subagent calls to direct Write/Edit/Bash-mutate calls should be >0.30 ... if <0.10, flag it explicitly"). Nothing currently surfaces this number to the agent, so the self-grade never happens. Add a tool-counter section to the system prompt that the agent sees on each turn: `tool counts so far this session: Write=N, Edit=M, subagent=K, ratio=K/(N+M+Bash_mutate)`. Visibility alone moves behavior — same mechanism as the context-mode throttle counter that already ships in ctx_search responses.
recommendations.evidence: subagent=18%, async=11% across 385 sessions; AGENTS.md mandates an explicit self-grade that the data shows is not happening; precedent for in-response counters already exists in this codebase (ctx_search throttle counter).
recommendations.concreteAction: Add a `session_tool_stats` block injected into every assistant turn after turn 3. Format: `<session_stats>writes=12 edits=8 bash_mutate=4 subagent=2 ratio=0.08 target=0.30</session_stats>`. Cheap to compute, impossible to ignore.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Directional — visibility nudges are well-documented in HCI but the effect size for LLM agents specifically is not measured here. Mechanism is plausible and cost is near-zero, which is why I'd still ship it.
recommendations.risk: Adds a few tokens per turn; negligible. Could be gamed by spurious subagent calls — pair with OG-1's gate to keep semantics honest.

recommendations.title: Resolve the context-mode vs pi-subagents tension at the system-prompt level, not the docs level
recommendations.description: AGENTS.md spends ~200 words resolving the conflict between context-mode's 4-tier `tool_selection_hierarchy` (which defaults everything to ctx_* in the parent) and pi-subagents' delegate-first posture. The system prompt the agent actually sees STILL says "context-mode active. Hierarchy: ctx_batch_execute > ctx_execute > ctx_execute_file > ctx_search" with no mention of subagent being level −1. The model reads the system prompt every turn and AGENTS.md once. Of course it reaches for ctx_batch_execute on implementation tasks — that's what the live hierarchy line tells it to do. Fix the live hierarchy line.
recommendations.evidence: workflow=0%, subagent=18% vs the explicit AGENTS.md rule "subagent dispatch is level −1"; the current context-mode system-prompt line shown in this very session lists four ctx_* tools and zero mention of subagent precedence.
recommendations.concreteAction: Edit the context-mode active-banner to: `Hierarchy for multi-file implementation work: subagent > ctx_batch_execute > ctx_execute > ctx_execute_file > ctx_search. For single-session processing: ctx_batch_execute > ctx_execute > ...`. One-line change, lives at injection time.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Strong mechanism (per-turn prompt beats per-session doc) plus visible artifact (the banner is right there in the system prompt). Not 0.9+ because we can't isolate how much of the 18% gap is attributable to this specific banner vs. other friction.
recommendations.risk: Slight risk of confusing users who configured context-mode expecting strict ctx_* primacy; document the change in the context-mode changelog.

recommendations.title: Instrument and publish the subagent-ratio metric per session
recommendations.description: We currently have aggregate counts (workflow=0, subagent=18%, async=11%) but no per-session ratio distribution, no breakdown by task type (feature/refactor/bugfix/conversation), and no view into WHICH sessions skipped orchestration. Without that, every fix above is a shot in the dark on impact sizing. Add a post-session record (or augment the existing one feeding this evidence pack) that emits `{ session_id, task_class, write_n, edit_n, bash_mutate_n, subagent_n, async_n, workflow_n, ratio }`. Then the next iteration of this analysis can target the worst-offending task classes specifically.
recommendations.evidence: The evidence pack provided to this analysis contained only aggregate percentages (workflow=0, subagent=18%, async=11%, N=385) with no per-session detail, no task-class breakdown, and no time series — the very gaps that make every recommendation above carry residual uncertainty.
recommendations.concreteAction: Extend whatever pipeline produced the 385-session aggregate to emit per-session JSONL with the fields listed above. Add a `pi sessions analyze --orchestration` CLI command. Re-run this specialist analysis after one week of new data.
recommendations.confidenceRationale: Meta-recommendation, but high confidence: the evidence pack itself is the proof that observability is the bottleneck. Mechanism (you can't optimize what you can't see) is bulletproof. Capped below 0.9 only because impact is indirect — it enables better future fixes rather than fixing behavior directly.
recommendations.risk: Adds telemetry surface; respect existing privacy/local-only posture of pi by keeping the JSONL on-disk and opt-in for any upload.

result.headline: Across 6 specialists, the dominant signal is that pi's standing orders and best-practice rules live as prose but get ignored under tempo pressure — 681 failed-retry loops and 537 duplicate-arg replays across 385 sessions, workflow=0% adoption, subagent=18% (target >30%), parallel-call ratio=0.127. The highest-leverage fixes convert prose norms into harness-level gates and counters: a duplicate-call/failed-retry breaker, a PreToolUse orchestration gate, batched-tool prominence in tool descriptions, and verification that prompt caching is on the stable system-prompt prefix. Observability is the meta-bottleneck: the evidence pack itself lacked per-session cost and ratio data, so ship a cost+orchestration JSONL ledger to retire residual uncertainty on every other recommendation.

topRecommendations.title: Failed-retry loop breaker with hypothesis-change gate
topRecommendations.description: Track consecutive failures per (tool, target). After 3 deterministic failures on the same target, block the 4th call and inject a forced-reasoning turn: 'You have failed 3× on <target>. State a new hypothesis or escalate.' Distinguish transient errors (timeout/5xx/EAGAIN — free retry with backoff) from deterministic errors (ENOENT, EPERM, syntax — gate immediately). Source: LSP-3.
topRecommendations.evidence: 681 failed-retry loops corpus-wide (~1.77/session) — the single largest waste category in the pack. Mechanism (sunk-cost retry without hypothesis change) is documented across agent failure-mode literature.
topRecommendations.confidenceRationale: Highest single-pathology count in the pack; mechanically simple gate; specialist gave it 0.9 standalone and no other rec contradicts it.
topRecommendations.risk: Flaky-network retries get blocked if classifier mis-tags transient as deterministic. Mitigation: per-error-class allowlist; emit telemetry on every gate fire so policy is tunable.
topRecommendations.concreteAction: Add a per-(tool,target) failure counter to the harness. On 3rd deterministic failure, return a structured 'hypothesis-change required' response that the model must address in prose before the 4th call is permitted.
topRecommendations.expectedOutcome: Eliminate the bulk of 681 failed-retry loops; conservatively cut tail-session tool-call counts 10–20% and reduce $-per-session at p95+ proportionally.

topRecommendations.title: Duplicate-argument replay detector with cached-result inline and escalation
topRecommendations.description: Hash every tool call by (tool_name, normalized_args). On 2nd identical replay within a session, return the cached prior result + a 'duplicate suppressed' system note. On 3rd, hard-block and force a planning turn. On 4th, escalate to forced summarization/handoff. Allowlist non-idempotent tools (Bash, network fetches, time-sensitive reads). Source: LSP-2.
topRecommendations.evidence: 537 duplicate-arg replays across 385 sessions (~1.4/session, concentrated in long sessions). By definition zero new information for non-zero token cost.
topRecommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is unambiguous (identical args → identical result for pure tools), large N, no specialist contradiction.
topRecommendations.risk: Mis-allowlisted non-idempotent tools could return stale data. Mitigate with a per-tool idempotency flag; default Bash/fetch/MCP-network calls to non-cacheable.
topRecommendations.concreteAction: Implement a session-scoped LRU keyed by (tool, normalized_args) for idempotency-flagged tools (Read, Grep, find_files, ctx_search, ctx_execute_file). Inline cached result with a [cached] marker.
topRecommendations.expectedOutcome: Recover ~537 wasted calls × avg-token-cost across the corpus — directly trims input-token spend on the long-session tail and visibly shortens sessions that loop on the same Read/Grep.

topRecommendations.title: PreToolUse orchestration gate on session-first multi-file mutations
topRecommendations.description: Merge of OG-1 and SO-1. Add a `orchestration-gate` PreToolUse hook (same shape as context-mode's routing hook). When the FIRST Write/Edit/Bash-mutate of a session would touch >1 directory or create >1 new file AND the session has zero prior subagent dispatches, block the call. Return a structured remediation suggesting a scout/researcher async dispatch, with an explicit `--ack-skip-orchestration <reason>` bypass that is logged for self-grading.
topRecommendations.evidence: workflow=0%, subagent=18% vs AGENTS.md mandated >30% floor — 10× miss despite the rule being delivered as system-prompt prose in every session. context-mode's PreToolUse hook is precedent that hook-level enforcement works in this codebase.
topRecommendations.confidenceRationale: Two specialists independently arrived at the same fix with the same mechanism (prose loses to tempo). Capped <0.9 because we lack per-session task-class data; some skips may be legitimate single-file edits the heuristic would mis-fire on.
topRecommendations.risk: False positives on legitimate investigative or single-developer quick edits. Mitigate: fires only on session-first multi-file mutation; explicit bypass token; ship behind config flag and dial in over a week.
topRecommendations.concreteAction: Implement the hook against the existing extension hook surface. Detection heuristic: pending tool targets span >1 directory OR create >1 new file. Remediation message names /parallel-research, /parallel-context-build, or scout-async as cheapest unblock.
topRecommendations.expectedOutcome: Move subagent-dispatch ratio from 18% toward the AGENTS.md target of 30%+; cut parent-context bloat (and downstream cost) on the heaviest-cost session class (multi-file scaffolds done inline).

topRecommendations.title: Promote batched tools in their descriptions and add real-tool few-shot examples
topRecommendations.description: Merge of PB-2 and PB-4. (a) Replace the system-prompt's fictional 'example_complex_tool' batching example with 2–3 examples using REAL tools from this harness (parallel Read×3; Grep+find_files+Read; ctx_batch_execute). Annotate each: 'these are independent → one block.' (b) Edit tool descriptions for ctx_batch_execute, fff_multi_grep, and web_search to lead with the batch use-case and add 'Prefer this over single-call X when you have ≥2 independent items.' Add to ctx_execute description: 'For ≥2 independent commands, use ctx_batch_execute instead.'
topRecommendations.evidence: 0.127 parallel/serial ratio across 385 sessions despite explicit directive and existing batched tools — affordances exist, steering does not. Few-shot effects on tool-call formatting are very well documented; current example uses a fake tool name.
topRecommendations.confidenceRationale: Two specialists converge; mechanism (description-as-discovery-surface + few-shot pattern-match) is direct and zero-implementation-cost; the current example is demonstrably weak.
topRecommendations.risk: Users with single-item queries could get pushed toward awkward 1-element arrays; mitigate with 'use single form only when N=1' hint in descriptions.
topRecommendations.concreteAction: Edit `pi`'s tool registry: prepend a 1-line batch-preference sentence to ctx_batch_execute / fff_multi_grep / web_search descriptions. Replace the example block in the system prompt with 2 real-tool examples.
topRecommendations.expectedOutcome: Lift parallel/serial ratio from 0.127 toward 0.25+; proportional cut in wall-clock latency on read-heavy turns and modest input-token savings via fewer turn boundaries.

topRecommendations.title: Verify and enable prompt caching on the stable system-prompt prefix
topRecommendations.description: The system prompt in this session alone is ~30KB (skill listings, AGENTS.md, tool descriptions). Across 385 sessions × multi-turn, re-sending this uncached is a meaningful share of input-token spend. Anthropic prompt caching cuts cached-prefix input cost ~90%. Verify pi's Anthropic client wrapper sets `cache_control: {type:'ephemeral'}` on the stable system-prompt block and the skills/AGENTS.md region; add a unit test that the cached prefix hash is stable across turns. Source: C5.
topRecommendations.evidence: Direct observation: skills+AGENTS.md+tool-descriptions block is ~30KB and identical turn-over-turn within a session. Provider pricing for cached prefix is documented at ~10% of base input cost.
topRecommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism + pricing well-understood. Confidence held below 0.9 because we cannot confirm from evidence whether caching is already enabled — could be no-op.
topRecommendations.risk: None if already enabled (it's a verification); if newly enabled, watch for cache invalidation from any per-turn-injected dynamic block.

synth.headline: Across 6 specialists, the dominant signal is that pi's standing orders and best-practice rules live as prose but get ignored under tempo pressure — 681 failed-retry loops and 537 duplicate-arg replays across 385 sessions, workflow=0% adoption, subagent=18% (target >30%), parallel-call ratio=0.127. The highest-leverage fixes convert prose norms into harness-level gates and counters: a duplicate-call/failed-retry breaker, a PreToolUse orchestration gate, batched-tool prominence in tool descriptions, and verification that prompt caching is on the stable system-prompt prefix. Observability is the meta-bottleneck: the evidence pack itself lacked per-session cost and ratio data, so ship a cost+orchestration JSONL ledger to retire residual uncertainty on every other recommendation.

topRecommendations.title: Failed-retry loop breaker with hypothesis-change gate
topRecommendations.description: Track consecutive failures per (tool, target). After 3 deterministic failures on the same target, block the 4th call and inject a forced-reasoning turn: 'You have failed 3× on <target>. State a new hypothesis or escalate.' Distinguish transient errors (timeout/5xx/EAGAIN — free retry with backoff) from deterministic errors (ENOENT, EPERM, syntax — gate immediately). Source: LSP-3.
topRecommendations.evidence: 681 failed-retry loops corpus-wide (~1.77/session) — the single largest waste category in the pack. Mechanism (sunk-cost retry without hypothesis change) is documented across agent failure-mode literature.
topRecommendations.confidenceRationale: Highest single-pathology count in the pack; mechanically simple gate; specialist gave it 0.9 standalone and no other rec contradicts it.
topRecommendations.risk: Flaky-network retries get blocked if classifier mis-tags transient as deterministic. Mitigation: per-error-class allowlist; emit telemetry on every gate fire so policy is tunable.
topRecommendations.concreteAction: Add a per-(tool,target) failure counter to the harness. On 3rd deterministic failure, return a structured 'hypothesis-change required' response that the model must address in prose before the 4th call is permitted.
topRecommendations.expectedOutcome: Eliminate the bulk of 681 failed-retry loops; conservatively cut tail-session tool-call counts 10–20% and reduce $-per-session at p95+ proportionally.

topRecommendations.title: Duplicate-argument replay detector with cached-result inline and escalation
topRecommendations.description: Hash every tool call by (tool_name, normalized_args). On 2nd identical replay within a session, return the cached prior result + a 'duplicate suppressed' system note. On 3rd, hard-block and force a planning turn. On 4th, escalate to forced summarization/handoff. Allowlist non-idempotent tools (Bash, network fetches, time-sensitive reads). Source: LSP-2.
topRecommendations.evidence: 537 duplicate-arg replays across 385 sessions (~1.4/session, concentrated in long sessions). By definition zero new information for non-zero token cost.
topRecommendations.confidenceRationale: Mechanism is unambiguous (identical args → identical result for pure tools), large N, no specialist contradiction.
topRecommendations.risk: Mis-allowlisted non-idempotent tools could return stale data. Mitigate with a per-tool idempotency flag; default Bash/fetch/MCP-network calls to non-cacheable.
topRecommendations.concreteAction: Implement a session-scoped LRU keyed by (tool, normalized_args) for idempotency-flagged tools (Read, Grep, find_files, ctx_search, ctx_execute_file). Inline cached result with a [cached] marker.
topRecommendations.expectedOutcome: Recover ~537 wasted calls × avg-token-cost across the corpus — directly trims input-token spend on the long-session tail and visibly shortens sessions that loop on the same Read/Grep.

topRecommendations.title: PreToolUse orchestration gate on session-first multi-file mutations
topRecommendations.description: Merge of OG-1 and SO-1. Add a `orchestration-gate` PreToolUse hook (same shape as context-mode's routing hook). When the FIRST Write/Edit/Bash-mutate of a session would touch >1 directory or create >1 new file AND the session has zero prior subagent dispatches, block the call. Return a structured remediation suggesting a scout/researcher async dispatch, with an explicit `--ack-skip-orchestration <reason>` bypass that is logged for self-grading.

topRecommendations.confidenceRationale: Two specialists independently arrived at the same fix with the same mechanism (prose loses to tempo). Capped <0.9 because we lack per-session task-class data; some skips may be legitimate single-file edits the heuristic would mis-fire on.
topRecommendations.risk: False positives on legitimate investigative or single-developer quick edits. Mitigate: fires only on session-first multi-file mutation; explicit bypass token; ship behind config flag and dial in over a week.
topRecommendations.concreteAction: Implement the hook against the existing extension hook surface. Detection heuristic: pending tool targets span >1 directory OR create >1 new file. Remediation message names /parallel-research, /parallel-context-build, or scout-async as cheapest unblock.
topRecommendations.expectedOutcome: Move subagent-dispatch ratio from 18% toward the AGENTS.md target of 30%+; cut parent-context bloat (and downstream cost) on the heaviest-cost session class (multi-file scaffolds done inline).

Across 385 sessions × multi-turn, re-sending this uncached is a meaningful share of input-token spend. Anthropic prompt caching cuts cached-prefix input cost ~90%. topRecommendations.title: Block interactive-TTY commands at the Bash tool boundary

topRecommendations.concreteAction: Flip the schema default for `async` in the subagent tool definition. Update the in-system-prompt guideline that says 'async (default: false)'. Bump dispatched skills' minor version with a migration note.
